title: Upcoming Webinar on Lifeguard Negligence and Legal Rights Announced By Aquatic Attorneys
text:
Upcoming Webinar on Lifeguard Negligence and Legal Rights Announced By Aquatic Attorneys By: Press Advantage March 19, 2025 at 18:40 PM EDT Miami, FL – Lifeguards serve as the first line of defense in preventing drowning incidents and ensuring swimmer safety. However, when lifeguards fail in their duties due to negligence, the consequences can be devastating. Aquatic Attorneys , a division of The Haggard Law Firm specializing in drowning and near-drowning cases, is hosting an upcoming webinar on lifeguard negligence, providing families, legal professionals, and community leaders with essential knowledge on water safety laws and victim advocacy. The webinar’s date is to be determined, and registration details will be announced soon.
The Lifeguard Negligence and Legal Rights Webinar will cover the dangers of lifeguard inattention, poor training, and emergency response failures. This educational event will explore legal avenues available to victims and families seeking justice. Attendees will gain insight into how lifeguard negligence occurs, what safety measures should be in place, and what legal steps can be taken when an incident occurs due to lifeguard failure.
Michael Haggard, Esq., a nationally recognized advocate for drowning victims and managing attorney at The Haggard Law Firm, emphasizes the importance of legal accountability in cases involving negligent lifeguards. “Families and individuals trust lifeguards to protect them in aquatic environments, and when that trust is broken due to inattention or inadequate training, the results can be catastrophic,” said Haggard. “Through this webinar, we aim to empower families and communities with information that can help prevent these tragedies and hold those responsible accountable.”
Lifeguard negligence occurs when an individual entrusted with supervising a body of water fails to take appropriate action to prevent drowning or injury. This may include inattention, distraction, lack of proper training, delayed emergency response, or failure to enforce pool safety regulations. When such negligence leads to injury or death, families have the legal right to seek justice and compensation.
The webinar will cover a series of topics including:
Identifying Lifeguard Negligence – Understanding how lapses in supervision and response contribute to drowning incidents.
Legal Rights of Victims – Exploring how families can pursue claims and seek justice when negligence leads to injury or death.
Drowning Prevention Strategies – Learning about safety measures that should be implemented at pools, waterparks, and beaches.
Holding Negligent Parties Accountable – Examining legal actions against facilities, employers, and individuals responsible for lifeguard failures.
Q&A Session with Legal Experts – Providing attendees with an opportunity to ask specific legal questions regarding lifeguard negligence cases.
Drowning remains a major public health crisis, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reporting that it is one of the leading causes of accidental death in the U.S. for children under five years old. Lifeguards serve as the first and often last line of defense against these tragedies, making it imperative that they are properly trained, equipped, and focused on their responsibilities.
Common signs of lifeguard negligence include:
Failure to Monitor Swimmers – Lifeguards must remain vigilant and continuously scan their designated areas to identify swimmers in distress.
Distracted Behavior – Using mobile phones, engaging in conversations, or failing to maintain proper surveillance.
Lack of Proper Training – Insufficient knowledge of CPR, rescue techniques, and emergency response protocols.
Delayed Action in Emergencies – Hesitation or failure to respond immediately in life-threatening situations.
Inadequate Staffing – Having too few lifeguards for large or crowded swimming areas, increasing the likelihood of incidents.
Aquatic Attorneys provides legal assistance to victims of drowning and near-drowning incidents caused by lifeguard negligence. Families who have suffered due to inadequate supervision can pursue compensation for medical expenses, emotional distress, and other damages. Legal action can also help enforce higher safety standards at aquatic facilities, preventing future tragedies.
“Our legal team has extensive experience handling drowning-related cases and advocating for stronger water safety policies,” Haggard added. “By taking action against negligent lifeguards and their employers, we work to create safer aquatic environments for all.”
Attendees of the upcoming Lifeguard Negligence and Legal Rights Webinar will leave with a comprehensive understanding of their legal options, as well as actionable steps they can take to ensure accountability and promote stronger water safety measures.
